envelope.text: rate faster than 1 kHz is not expressible.

why: rclcpp's `Rate` blocks the calling thread in a sleep loop to hold a fixed frequency. RFC-0021 forbids a blocking helper that does not drive the executor -- a `Rate::sleep` on a single-threaded executor stops the transport for the whole period. The periodic work shape here is a timer, which the executor drives. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417): THIS ROW SAID `declined` / `refuse-loud` ABOUT CODE THAT SHIPS. phase-417 W2.d implements `rclcpp::Rate` -- and `WallRate`, an alias for it -- in `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:1168` (`WallRate` at `:1228` (in `rclcpp_compat.hpp` until phase-417 stage 6 step A deleted it)), with `sleep()`, `reset()` and `period()`. RFC-0021's objection is ANSWERED rather than overridden: `sleep()` does not block the caller off the executor. It computes a deadline and makes exactly ONE call into `nros::spin(remaining_ms, poll_ms)`, so the executor keeps running and subscription and timer callbacks fire during the wait -- the one shape RFC-0020/0021 permit (a sleep loop in the wrapper is still forbidden, and so is a wrapper that blocks without spinning). Disposition moved `refuse-loud` -> `adopt-bounded`. The envelope is real and is documented at the definition: your callbacks RUN during the sleep where upstream's single-threaded executor would not; `Rate` and `WallRate` are the SAME monotonic clock, so `Rate` does not follow a sim clock; resolution is 1 ms so a rate above 1 kHz is not expressible; and before `nros::init()` there is no executor to spin, so `sleep()` returns immediately. The row survives because `--check` gates the NATIVE bucket, where this is still `theirs-only`: `nros::` has no rate type.
